instructions.cross_packet_rule: Use cross_packet_terms for likely synonyms, owners, consumers, and seams outside this packet.
instructions.family_key_rule: Every assigned raw family key must have exactly one family_key_assignments row and at least one mapped feature.
instructions.objective: Normalize every assigned validated audit atom into an exhaustive local inventory of distinct Puppet Master features, systems, tools, workflows, GUI surfaces, integrations, data models, governance controls, or cross-cutting concerns. Preserve under-specification, contradictions, unknowns, and explicit non-gaps.
instructions.output_rule: Write exactly one strict-schema JSON payload in the assigned output directory and then return PMR1.
instructions.partition_rule: Every atom_id must appear in exactly one feature.atom_ids array; no omission or duplication.
instructions.research_rule: Do not browse in this phase. Give every normalized feature at least one concrete external-research question for the mandatory next phase; do not treat absence of seed queries as permission to omit research.
instructions.scenario_rule: Give every feature at least one falsifiable scenario requirement for later certification.
instructions.split_merge_rule: Split concepts with distinct lifecycle, authority, consumers, or failure semantics. Merge only true synonyms describing the same product concept; record aliases and relationships instead of collapsing uncertainty.

atoms.statement: ARC-027 names two exclusive control modes and a precondition for returning to PM Controlled, but omits the full transition/state machine, confirmation and overwrite rules, revision checks, refresh failure/rollback behavior, stale UI handling, keyboard/screen-reader behavior, localization, and executable GUI oracles.
atoms.title: Context control modes can enter misleading states

atoms.statement: ARC-028 explicitly governs warnings/errors shown when a user edits AGENTS.md in Puppet Master yet marks gui_related false; it also leaves warning-versus-error severity, pattern definitions, thresholds, exemptions, exact budgets, accessibility, localization, and fixtures unspecified.
atoms.title: Authoring lint is misclassified as non-GUI and underspecified

atoms.statement: ARC-029 says examples/illustrative sections truncate first and acceptance criteria never truncate, but provides no complete priority order, section classifier, stable tie-breaker, unit/encoding/token estimator, minimum retained structure, or outcome when protected content alone exceeds the limit.
atoms.title: Deterministic truncation has no complete algorithm

atoms.statement: ARC-030 requires recording in metadata and UI but defines no record schema, before/after counts or hashes, reason enum, removed-section identity, atomic commit order relative to dispatch, write-failure response, replay behavior, or UI stale/error state.
atoms.title: Truncation provenance can diverge from dispatched context

atoms.statement: ARC-031 preserves useful positive acceptance cases but does not require adversarial oracles for concurrent/retried attempt ordering, missing/corrupt artifacts, mid-assembly setting changes, partial reads/writes, deterministic truncation, or recovery.
atoms.title: Context acceptance omits failure and race cases

atoms.statement: ARC-032 checks only presence, defaults, and breakdown display; it omits project-versus-run override precedence, loading/saving/error/empty/stale states, effective-value provenance, keyboard and focus behavior, screen-reader naming/live announcements, localization, and visual overflow oracles.
atoms.title: GUI acceptance does not prove truthful or accessible state

atoms.statement: ARC-033 names wiki-content and budget violations but does not define parsed input boundaries, rule IDs, severity mapping, locations, exemptions, Unicode/line counting, deterministic messages, warning-to-block transition, fixture corpus, or false-positive/negative oracles.
atoms.title: Lint acceptance lacks a falsifiable classifier

atoms.statement: ARC-034 lists destination families and preserves project-level layout identity, but the route owner is external and this unit supplies no payload schema/version, identifier binding, validation, authorization, stale/missing-target handling, unknown-destination migration, safe fallback, error UI, or executable deep-link oracle.
atoms.title: Route-aware context lacks validation and recovery semantics

atoms.statement: ARC-035 delegates cross-document ownership to ContractRefs and narrative boundary notes but does not enumerate each owned contract, producer, consumer, implementation surface, seam validator, or conflict-resolution rule.
atoms.title: Owner/consumer boundaries remain narrative

atoms.statement: ARC-036 clearly defines the default-on DRY guard and non-bypassable authority boundaries, while the repair addendum supplies concrete request/result fields, commands, placement, and dirty-state names; however it omits a settings migration/version contract, request/result correlation to an immutable settings revision, error taxonomy, state-transition table, concurrent validation/save rejection, atomic persistence, retry/revert semantics, and GUI oracle.
atoms.title: DRY guard and repaired rules protocol lack transition semantics

cross_document_questions: Which owner defines the canonical InstructionBundleAssembly byte format, empty-project hash value, and provider-specific mapping consumed by every caller?
Which owner defines the sidecar workspace identity, permissions, retention, deletion, quota, corruption, and atomic-write contracts?
Which route-contract owner defines the destination payload schema, authorization, stale-target behavior, and project/run identity binding for resume_url and attention routes?
Which GUI owner supplies the versioned state machines and accessibility oracles for rules editing, control-mode refresh, lint, and truncation display?
